Verdicts.Verdict:
Reviewed against the approved spec by the authority. Review 0 findings; WriteEvidence scope audit 15 paths 0 findings; attempt-pair audit 3 pairs 0 findings; scope audit not-run on a clean tree, the honest F27 case. Verified independently: suite 1476 pass 0 fail, validate:ci exit 0, grace-status.ts still contains the word commit zero times, and no AC-SUITE-AND-LINT element exists in either artifact.
DISCLOSURE 1, TWO ROADMAP CLAIMS FAILED CONSTRUCTION, RECORDED AS F83. Seventh and eighth in this phase. P2.6 was already true at HEAD: status recommends refresh and never mentions committing, so there was nothing to build, and the rule as stated is the undifferentiated one F7 already refuted - never-commit is right for unexplained drift and wrong for the approved-contract-drift hard stop. P2.4's credit rule could not match its own subject: an archived bundle's ObservedWriteScope still spells the active path while its bytes live under archive, so exact matching credits stray src paths and misses the moved bundle, leaving the very nag the step exists to remove. Two overclaims in the same sentence were also corrected: OWS credit is permanent, so any later dirty edit to a once-approved path becomes explained - a real narrowing the step denied - and the post-bootstrap nag belongs to P4.2, not here. All corrections were amended into the roadmap before approval.
DISCLOSURE 2, THIS BUNDLE DEMONSTRATES THE F82 REPAIR IT DEFINES. AC-SUITE-AND-CI is Satisfies-linked to T-004, whose verification runs the suite and validate:ci and contains no lint command; post-archive lint is verdict evidence and no AC-SUITE-AND-LINT element was authored - measured zero in both artifacts. The executor also found the trap inside F82's own prescription: a second close-time criterion that no task satisfies raises change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped, so both shapes F82 suggested are unclosable and verdict evidence is the only workable split. A finding that prescribes a repair inherits the obligation to check the repair is closable; mine did not.
DISCLOSURE 3, AN ADJUDICATION GIVEN BEFORE EXECUTION AT THE EXECUTOR'S REQUEST. It asked whether the archive-alias red had to be red at pre-change HEAD, and said to stop it before T-001 rather than at plan review if I disagreed. I did not: at original HEAD an archived path is unexplained for the same reason a src match is, so reddening both there would make the second fail for the first's cause - the F68 collision. Before its production edit means before T-002's rewrite. The recorded red confirms it failed as an alias failure while applied credit was already green.
DISCLOSURE 4, F84 CORRECTS A DESIGN NOTE IN THE PLAN I APPROVED. D5 sequenced T-001 as pass then bounding pins. The executor inverted it deliberately and reported it, correctly: cursor attempt pass snapshots WriteEvidence when it runs, so a pass recorded before the pins captures a tree missing the files that bound the task's claim, and the scope audit reading that snapshot would never see them. Pins belong inside the pass snapshot; the order is red, production, pins, pass. The same report also disclosed that T-002's other-suffix case was described as part of the recorded red while being green at fail-record time - a bound, not a red, and F80's rule from the other direction.
DISCLOSURE 5, AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE APPROVED SPEC. Its Summary presents P2.6 as work this bundle does, while its Problem and AC-NEXT-ACTION treat it as already true and exempt under F45. The executor treated it as a pin, matching F83, and reported the disagreement rather than resolving it silently. Same class as F75. Not amended - the artifact is approved and the executed behaviour is the honest reading.
DISCLOSURE 6, A STANDING CONTRADICTION NOW LOAD-BEARING. The shipped ngrace-execute skill still assigns final assertions, apply and archive to the executor, while this roadmap's practice makes the close authority-owned. Every dispatch in this phase has contradicted the skill on that split and the executor has flagged it each time. Recorded in F84 and owed to whichever bundle next opens that skill; it is a decision, not a drift.
DISCLOSURE 7, WHAT REMAINS UNPINNED. The alias against an archived Glob - the fixture is File-only, and every archived Glob in this repository is the run directory under the active spelling. Windows separators: porcelain lists are POSIX-normalized and the alias helper never uses the platform separator, but this host cannot observe the difference, so CI is the only observer (F73). No applied-glob fixture, so a wide Glob narrowing is uncharacterized.
DISCLOSURE 8. decisions.md was written during the open window - F83 before execution, F84 mid-window - each in its own commit ahead of the implementation commit, and staged by filename rather than with add -A after that error was caught on the previous bundle. It is outside every bundle's ObservedWriteScope by design, and the scope audit reads working-tree porcelain, so committing removed those edits from the audit's view rather than clearing them.
